solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sure winner Ken found drunk in pub

indicators.note: in places the jumbled name inside the word for a pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of Ken are reeling about in a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Ken, drunk in the pub, is reckoned a certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles the name, and 'in' sets the result inside the pub. A banker is also the puzzle's theme: several answers are famous bankers.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting slang a banker is a certainty, a selection expected to come in every time.

clue.text: GB dealer generates capital

indicators.note: generates suggests the letters of GB dealer produce something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A British dealer turns out capital, as if cash were being made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'generates' rearranges GBDEALER. 'capital' suggests money, fitting the banking theme, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital city of Serbia.

clue.text: Something forsaken by Tiger frolicking in unclothed situation?

indicators.note: in places the frolicking letters within the word for being unclothed

parts.note: being in the nude is an unclothed situation

indicators.note: frolicking says the letters of Tiger are larking about into a new order

explanation.surface: Tiger, frolicking with nothing on, gives something up.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfer Tiger Woods famously declined to identify simply as black, calling himself 'Cablinasian'; that is what he forsook. 'frolicking' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Negritude is a sense of black identity and pride, which Tiger Woods declined to claim as his sole heritage.

clue.text: The point is, brutal person suffers decapitation

indicators.note: suffers decapitation means the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a beast is a brutal person

explanation.surface: The point is that a brute has his head cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four points of the compass.

clue.text: Strong man, 50, captivated by womanly signals

parts.note: her is the womanly pronoun

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive inside the following words

parts.note: cues are signals
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old strongman is charmed by a woman's hints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivated by' puts the Roman fifty inside the womanly signals, between the U and the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules is the hero of Greek and Roman myth famous for his great strength.

clue.text: Corrected earth people on half-hearted action

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: half-hearted means the double letter at the heart of the word for action is cut to half, one letter

parts.note: a deed is an action

explanation.surface: Something on earth was put right by people taking half-hearted action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of the two letters at the heart of the word for action. 'on' is only a link here, joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct it, so emended means put right.

clue.text: Chap with poodle mistaken for sea creature

indicators.note: mistaken suggests the letters of chap and poodle have been got wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A man with his poodle is mistaken for something from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaken' rearranges CHAP plus POODLE, with 'with' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cephalopod, such as an octopus or squid, is a sea mollusc with tentacles.

clue.text: Fish and duck produce strange language

parts.note: a ling is a fish of the cod family
in cricket a duck, a score of nothing, is O

explanation.surface: Fish and duck together come up with an odd tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a language or jargon that sounds foreign or odd to the listener.

clue.text: Sandy also going to hold back in quarrel

indicators.note: to hold means the remaining letters are placed around the next piece
going means a piece is removed from the name

parts.note: and means also
hind means back or rear, as in hind legs

explanation.surface: Sandy is also set to hold back in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' strips 'also' out of the name, leaving SY, and 'to hold' wraps that round the word for back.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindy is a noisy disturbance or row, so it is a quarrel.

clue.text: Renowned for fat-reduced sumo wrestling

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short, losing its final letter
wrestling suggests the letters of sumo grapple into a new order

explanation.surface: A sumo wrestler, slimmed down, is renowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts FAT to FA, and 'wrestling' rearranges SUMO into MOUS. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous and renowned are synonyms: both mean widely known and celebrated.

clue.text: Make provision where member has missed appointment

parts.note: a leg is a member, a limb
someone who has missed an appointment is late, so the phrase reads as is late

explanation.surface: Making arrangements when a member of the committee fails to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a scene: the member (LEG) IS LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, setting down provision for something.

clue.text: Scheming swindler with money staked virtually nothing

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so each word loses its last letter

parts.note: a pony is slang for twenty-five pounds, a common sum staked on a bet
zip means nothing

explanation.surface: A fraudster puts up a stake that amounts to almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims the last letter from both PONY and ZIP, leaving PON and ZI.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ponzi was a 1920s fraudster whose scam paid early investors with later investors' money.

clue.text: Economies face this one with urgent demand for cash on every side

indicators.note: on every side means the letters surround the next piece

parts.note: a run on a bank is a rush of customers all demanding their money
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Economies face disaster when everyone urgently wants their money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on every side' puts I inside RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin, total collapse or bankruptcy, is what failing economies are threatened with.

clue.text: 1 across shilling did secure a certain amount of money

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling, an old British coin worth twelve pence

indicators.note: secure means hold firmly, so the letters of did hold the next pieces
a certain amount of means only part of the word is used, its end dropped

explanation.surface: A shilling did secure a sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was an old British coin. 'secure' sets A plus MON, the start of money cut down by 'certain amount of', inside 'did'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Diamond was chief executive of Barclays bank, so he fits the theme answer at 1 across.

clue.text: Beaten legion ever in the shade

indicators.note: beaten suggests the letters of legion and ever have been knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A defeated legion is still in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' rearranges LEGION plus EVER, with 'in the' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive green is a dull yellowish-green colour, a shade of green.

clue.text: Man's capital with us keeping pound in 1 across

parts.note: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the letters of the paper hold the next pieces

parts.note: us is the setter's newspaper, the Financial Times, FT
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Man's capital keeps pound in the bank with us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the Financial Times speaking of itself. 'keeping' holds the pound sign's letter and 'in' inside the paper's initials. The Isle of Man lies between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas Flint was chairman of HSBC, so he is a banker as the theme answer at 1 across requires.

clue.text: Cartoon poodle seen from rear in very poor drawing

indicators.note: seen from rear says the hidden letters are read backwards
in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words very poor drawing

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cartoon dog looks rather badly drawn from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'seen' into the definition; it belongs with 'from rear' as the reversal signal. YPOORD runs through 'very poor drawing' and reads backwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Droopy is the lugubrious cartoon dog from MGM shorts, so the clue's dog stands for him.

clue.text: We at bar drunkenly sit round to provide foundation in authority

indicators.note: round means the letters for sit go around the next pieces

parts.note: to pose is to sit for a portrait or photograph

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests the letters of bar stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Drunk at the bar, we sit around building a political following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' scrambles the drinking place, and 'round' wraps the sitting word round 'We' plus that. 'at' and 'to provide' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A power base is the body of support from which someone draws their authority.

clue.text: Left as seen outside Troy, came to grief under one from Paris

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means the pieces that follow sit below the French word

parts.note: une is French for one

indicators.note: outside means the letters for came to grief go around the next piece

parts.note: died means came to grief
T is the abbreviation for troy weight

explanation.surface: Left as seen outside Troy, where a Greek hero met his end at the hands of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps 'came to grief' round the troy abbreviation, giving DITED, and 'under' sets that below the French word in this down answer. Paris pretends to be the Trojan prince who killed Achilles.
explanation.definitionFit: Unedited copy is left as first seen, with no changes made.

clue.text: 1 across Mr Envy at odds with top man

indicators.note: at odds suggests the letters of Mr Envy are out of order

parts.note: a king is the top man

explanation.surface: Mr Envy is at odds with the man at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at odds' rearranges MRENVY into MERVYN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mervyn King was Governor of the Bank of England, a banker as the theme answer requires.

clue.text: Insane person Dicky can't use

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so the letters are in bad shape and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A madman can't use a weak and faulty thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' is British slang for unsound, as in a dicky heart; it rearranges CANTUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcase is a slang word for a crazy person.

clue.text: See 25
Hindu god sustains cut about middle of knee

indicators.note: about means the cut goes around the next piece

parts.note: a gash is a cut

indicators.note: middle of takes the letters at the centre of the word, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: A Hindu deity holds up with a cut around the knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the centre letters of knee, and 'about' wraps the cut round them. 'sustains' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganesh is the elephant-headed Hindu god of wisdom and new beginnings.

clue.text: Spot one sitting inside massive building

indicators.note: inside means the letters go within the word for the building

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
an MP, a Member of Parliament, sits in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: One spot is seated in a great big building.
explanation.walkthrough: A Member of Parliament sits in the Commons, so 'one sitting' is that abbreviation; 'inside' puts it in the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimple is a spot on the skin.

clue.text: Say 1 across v 1 across where international female surrounded by darkness in Gulf

indicators.note: surrounded by means the female letter is placed inside the word for darkness

parts.note: night is darkness
G is an abbreviation for Gulf, as on maps

explanation.surface: An international woman, shrouded in darkness in the Gulf, finds bankers fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' puts F inside NIGHT, after its N. 'Say 1 across v 1 across' means banker against banker, a fight within one group.
explanation.definitionFit: Infighting is conflict among members of the same group, like one banker battling another.

clue.text: See 15 across
Former 1 across fellow in shame perhaps given right result

parts.note: someone in shame may go red in the face
good means right, as in a good answer
a win is a result

explanation.surface: A fellow who was ashamed is given the right result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link. In football slang a result means a win, so RESULT gives WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Goodwin was chief executive of the Royal Bank of Scotland until it collapsed in 2008.

clue.text: See 19 across
Potato starter and starchy food served in Jordan?

indicators.note: starter means the first letter of the word

parts.note: rice is a starchy food

explanation.surface: A potato starter and rice are served up in a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jordan' looks like the country, but it is the stage name of the British model and TV personality Katie Price.
explanation.definitionFit: Katie Price, a British glamour model and celebrity, worked under the name Jordan.

clue.text: Aggressor sets Alsatians loose

indicators.note: loose says the letters of Alsatians run free into a new order

explanation.surface: An attacker lets his German shepherd dogs off the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges ALSATIANS; 'sets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is someone who attacks another, an aggressor.

clue.text: Old love had disposition to get out

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, an old love
to have a disposition towards something is to tend to it, so had a disposition is tended

explanation.surface: A former partner was inclined to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Extended means stretched out at full length, like a ladder pulled out.

clue.text: Film all may see with mortal sin admitted

parts.note: an A certificate was an old British film rating that children could see with an adult
greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A family film is let in with a deadly sin.
explanation.walkthrough: A was an old British film certificate; children could see an A film if an adult went with them. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed and admitted both mean conceded, as when someone accepts a point is true.
